title: Supersede law corpus
description: Language-agnostic decision tables of the supersede law (design §3, §22.1). `inputs`: which replacement an operation takes. A withdrawal is admitted for every operation. An input is admitted when it is an operation of the document's schema in its canonical encoding that plans no foreign steps; an operation that plans foreign steps takes no input but its own recorded one. An admitted withdrawal folds its target as a no-op, an admitted input folds in its place, and a refused one folds the target as a no-op carrying one fatal `mutation.invariant` message — at every fold site, on every replica. `units`: which operations belong to a cross-artifact unit. An operation that plans foreign steps and whose plan on the projection before it is not empty changed other documents too; an operation of `transaction` origin is such a step of another document's operation. The unit is named by the gesture's group where the replica holds one, else by the operation. A supersession naming an operation of a unit is refused with `history.unit-spans-documents` and records nothing; every other operation is its own unit.

original.description: Whether the recorded operation plans foreign steps.

replacement.description: `withdrawn`; `recorded`: the operation's own recorded input; `plain` / `foreignStep`: another operation of the schema, planning no or some foreign steps; `otherSchema`: an operation named under another schema; `garbage`: bytes that are no operation.

folds.description: What every fold site folds for the target.

operation.description: `plain`; `planner`: plans foreign steps, its plan on the projection before it is empty; `foreignPlanner`: its plan there has a step.

group.description: Whether the replica holds a gesture group for the operation.

unit.description: `none`: its own unit; `group` / `operation`: a cross-artifact unit named by the group or by the operation.

supersede.description: What authoring a supersession of the operation answers.
